_about: Marden (161189, priest_prince_playable): rough-spoken heretic priest; polite only when acting. Translated from the game's Japanese. Global names/terms: Marden, the House of Oxtan (エイトラン), the House of Kwetur (フォーラー), the House of Sextan, Varen, Azrail, Yuwel, Vyron, Orvelle, Libram, Razelt, Corinna, Hans, Liesel, Denah, the Church of Farlana, Devourer of Stars (星喰い), Abyssal Parasite, Star Augurs, Purgers, Yuni, the Farlands, Palpebra, Starview Village. Own: Lost (ロスト), "the Guiding Hand" (導きの手), Parasite Abyss (skill name kept from units.json).
profile: Second son of the House of Oxtan, the eighth knightly house of the Kingdom of the Farlands. A high priest, and a corrupt one. A man who lost sight of the light and lost his star to rage and hatred, he met a star-devouring beast in the darkness.
titleCondition: Level Marden to 100 and obtain his Amity Scroll

speech.home/shoshinshomeino: The real Creator's already been killed, this thing's an evil god from another world, and it's sunk an entire world into the sea? ...It's nothing but stuff I don't want to believe.
speech.home/tanomukara: Please, just keep that Denah girl away from me! I seriously, absolutely cannot figure her out... What even IS she...!?
speech.home/isekainokoto: The more I learn about other worlds, the more my head hurts... What was it I even believed in... So stupid.
speech.home/yuni_iisakedayona: Yuni's a good drink, isn't it. I used to swipe it from the Swes kitchen and drink it all the time. ...Back when I could hang out with Libram without debts as an excuse.
speech.home/ha_razeruto: Huh? Prince Razelt was in this town too? ...Good thing we didn't run into each other... I deliberately avoided making his acquaintance. He's not someone who should get dragged into a swamp like mine.
speech.home/alk_kukkino: Alk. Could you teach me how to bake cookies? Lost keeps going on in my head about how the other terminals get sweets or whatever... I don't get it... What is this thing even saying...?
speech.home/nishitemo_parupeburano: Still, the sisters of Palpebra are, how do I put it... a lot to handle... How does Sister Liesel actually manage to spread the faith like that...? Should I be learning from her...?
speech.ally/join: Haha, another world. Another world, he says...? Everything's enough to make you question your sanity... seriously. What am I supposed to do...?
speech.ally/evolution: More than anything, I hated myself. I was an idiot who couldn't admit it. But... guidance for those in darkness. That's the kind of person I want to be--!

1.title: The Call of a Wish
1.summary: Marden wakes after sleeping for half a year, ever since the Purgers attacked Palpebra, and learns that the god he believed in is long gone, and that what he summoned was something else entirely. To save the despairing Marden, Varen and the others take him to Starview Village.

lines.6: The Houses are certainly in a difficult position-- but even so, they're your family, aren't they? ...Hm?
lines.9: I was a prodigal son. I've caused my father and brother nothing but trouble.
lines.13: Get some rest, Marden. At this rate you'll collapse on your own before any assassin gets to you.
lines.17: ......Doing this keeps me from thinking about unnecessary things.
lines.21: ...It's been half a year already. When I heard you'd nearly been assassinated, I could hardly believe my ears.
lines.25: If you don't intend to stop, why not make a deal, Marden?
lines.33: The House of Kwetur has already lost its sanity. That's how cornered they are. We can't leave it alone.
lines.36: Before they run wild again, we'll unravel their plot and hold them responsible. ...Our goal is the same, isn't it?
lines.44: ...You can't stop. But taking a step forward is hard too...?

lines.218: In fact, the time you collapsed coincides with when a Devourer of Stars, hunting the Purgers, appeared in Palpebra.

lines.265: We go to search for possibilities.
lines.269: Marden. You will go to Starview Village.

2.title: A Broken World
2.summary: Betrayed by his faith and drowning in drink, Marden wakes up in a room at an orphanage. Moved by the outlook of Corinna, who looks after the children, and facing himself through talking with Hans, a boy at the orphanage, Marden names the Devourer of Stars' terminal "Lost" and begins walking toward his goal.

lines.5: According to the founding myth... we were led from the land of lamentation to the Farlands.
lines.8: So this is the truth behind the myth... We're descendants of sinners who were purged--
lines.12: In every age, gods get twisted to suit people's convenience. You knew that, didn't you?
lines.16: God, the dragons, the world... broken from the very beginning...?
lines.20: But honestly, none of that matters either.
lines.24: Because you don't believe in god anyway, do you?
lines.27: Nothing ever guided me. All there was were things that refused to accept me and hurt me.
lines.30: ...So I'll destroy it. Cut out everything that warps and defiles the light. That's what you wanted, isn't it...?
lines.39: His Highness and I are different. Right?
lines.42: All I found from "talking" with my father and brother was a gouged-out wound. The me they damaged--
lines.47: Shut up!!! Shut up, shut up! Shut uuuup!!!
lines.60: Shut up, you dimwit. You plan to embarrass me any further...?
lines.62: Listen. Don't think about anything extra. You lot just shut up and do as you're told. If you've got time to use those tiny brains of yours--
lines.65: The one with the tiny brain... is you...
lines.72: It's 'cause people like you exist in this world... that I, that I--!!
lines.81: Ah... he's awake! Big sis Corinna!
lines.86: Thank goodness~~. Um... you're Marden, right...?
lines.94: Th-this is an orphanage we run. Stella helps out here a lot too--
lines.102: ...I-I'll keep the drinking a secret from the church!
lines.111: Um, if you'd like, I could at least listen to what's bothering you...? I'm a sister too, if only a lowly one!
lines.118: Why can you smile like that.
lines.122: Running an orphanage, you'd know it whether you like it or not. That there's no such thing as the guidance of the stars.
lines.130: It's embarrassing to admit, but I don't actually have all of Farlana's teachings memorized.
lines.133: I only studied to be a priest a little before I was taken in here. But I always loved the story of "the Guiding Hand".
lines.137: "...Even when the stars hide in a darkening sky, I can still reach out my hand. Take hold of the wandering hand..."
lines.142: Exactly. Because, look! Reaching out a hand is something you can do even if you're not a god.
lines.154: H-hey! Hans! Come out of there!
lines.157: Shut up! Everyone, everyone's a liar!! Just like my dad!!!
lines.159: He's the one who's wrong... but nobody... nobody listens to me...!!
lines.166: I'm... technically a priest too. I can at least listen...?
lines.169: ...Yeah. My dad never came to get me! He lied to me...!
lines.171: I'll never forgive liars...! Not even friends!! Never!!
lines.178: Then that's fine. You're allowed to be angry.
lines.182: But, Hans... isn't that different from being lonely?
lines.185: If so, then I'd better listen to what you have to say...
lines.189: That kid and I are the same.
lines.193: No, I'm even worse. I didn't want to look at the wounds my father and the rest gave me, so I ran all the way out here.
lines.196: "It won't get better"-- my ass. I just hated them. I just tried to kill them with a righteous excuse.
lines.199: ...I became exactly the thing I hate most.
lines.203: That's why you wanted to cut it out, right? The thing that damages you. Yourself?
lines.206: Then I'll devour you. I'll devour the stars. And build a world where everyone can walk toward the light!
lines.216: ...But I want you to help me.
lines.220: I want to be like Sister Corinna. That's exactly who I wanted to be accepted as...!
lines.224: Please...! Help me become something that simple...!
lines.228: I see. Then let's go with that.
lines.232: I understand your wish. Then I'll grant it. I am you, after all.
lines.237: Ha, haha... Seriously? What an honest evil god you turned out to be...

3.title: The Stars Guide Everyone
3.summary: Marden spends peaceful days preaching at the orphanage, until the House of Oxtan reaches out to strike. Resolving to face the darkness of the Farlands, Marden convinces Yuwel and the others, and begins scheming with Varen for the sake of his homeland's people.

lines.6: --O Goddess. Why do you not answer?
lines.8: In the land of lamentation, the one who reached out a hand to the lone priest grieving without an answer... was a band of shepherds.
lines.12: Of course, the shepherds were not gods. But it was in them that the priest saw god's will.
lines.15: To reach out a hand. That is the teaching of our Goddess of the Stars, and the most important thing of all.
lines.19: Everyone, be sure to help your friends when they're in trouble, okay? May the stars guide you.

2000080/1.19:
Second son of the House of Oxtan and a high priest, but at the same time a corrupt one who runs up debts on drink and women.

By leaking the relationship between the head house and the Star Augurs to Varen and the others, he tried to dig into the bad blood between the House of Oxtan and its head house, the House of Kwetur.

5000627/2.19:
It is characterized by a flavor in which the tartness and sweetness unique to apples are in perfect harmony. Easy to drink even for those who don't like alcohol, it is very popular among commoners.

On the other hand, nobles-- especially outside the Oinas domain-- consider it unfit for people of standing, making Marden, second son of the House of Oxtan, who loved it, a rare exception.

5000652/1.19:
One of the teachings handed down in the Church of Farlana, a principle that some factions consider the very core of the doctrine.

"Even beyond a darkening sky, the stars still shine. But people are not so strong that all can believe it. If there are those whom the starlight does not reach, who lose their way, reach out your own hand and take hold of the wandering hand. As a person, become a guide."

5000653/1.19:
A terminal of the Devourer of Stars that appeared before Marden, following the bond of the Abyssal Parasite that had latched onto him.
It has the function of granting the wishes of its human host.
At first, like the Abyssal Parasite, it resonated with Marden's destructive urges, but in the end it accepted his most fundamental wish.
To them, there is no good or evil in a wish. Nor, of course, in the means of granting it.
